Title: Diagnosis

Details: The failing test "testReflectionObjectCycle" is designed to test the reflection-based hash code building for objects that have cyclical references to each other (ReflectionTestCycleA and ReflectionTestCycleB). The test previously caused a `StackOverflowError` due to infinite recursion in the hash code calculation when encountering such cycles.

The method `HashCodeBuilder.reflectionHashCode(Object)` ultimately calls the more detailed `reflectionHashCode(int, int, T, boolean, Class<? super T>, String[])`, which performs the reflection on the object fields. This method delegates the recursive field processing to `reflectionAppend(Object, Class<?>, HashCodeBuilder, boolean, String[])`.

Inside `reflectionAppend`, before proceeding with reflecting fields of the object, there is a check to see if the object is already "registered" via `isRegistered(object)` which uses a ThreadLocal Registry set. If the object is registered (i.e., has been processed before in the current reflection cycle), it returns immediately to prevent infinite cycles.

If not registered, the object is registered by adding an `IDKey` wrapper for it to the registry before reflecting fields and building the hash code. After processing, the object is unregistered in a finally block to clean up.

The test asserts that after calling `a.hashCode()`, the registry is cleared (`getRegistry()` returns null), which would mean no memory leak or lingering references remain.

The current bug report indicates that the use of ThreadLocals in `HashCodeBuilder` (and also mentioned for `ToStringStyle`) to maintain registry sets causes memory leaks because the ThreadLocal registry is never properly removed or cleared, holding strong references which prevents garbage collection in container environments (such as webapps).

In relation to the test, if the registry is not cleaned up correctly or removed at the end of reflection-based hash code calculation, cyclic references between objects (like a->b and b->a) will cause the registry to hold references preventing proper garbage collection, potentially causing memory leaks.

Thus, while the current code of `reflectionAppend` properly unregisters objects after processing each one, the higher-level registry `HashCodeBuilder.getRegistry()` which backs the ThreadLocal is not cleared or removed after the full reflection cycle completes. The `register` and `unregister` methods only add or remove individual keys, but do not clear the ThreadLocal itself after the entire hash code computation.

This means multiple uses of reflectionHashCode may cause the ThreadLocal registry to accumulate or remain initialized without a clear removal mechanism, causing memory leaks which match the description in the bug report.

Summary: The recursive cycle detection and prevention in reflection-based hash code building via registry works correctly to avoid infinite recursion in the test. However, the ThreadLocal registry used to track visited objects is not properly cleared or removed after full computation, risking memory leaks in container environments, matching the current bug report.

Recent reports about Validate or TypeUtils are unrelated.

Hence the root cause is the missing removal/clearance of the ThreadLocal registry in HashCodeBuilder after reflection-based hashCode computations, which was exercised by the cyclical object test.

This diagnosis integrates the failing test cycle, the current bug report on ThreadLocal memory leaks, and confirmation from the inspected source code.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
